PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality defensive franchise with strong brand portfolio, 70-year dividend growth streak, and solid ROE (~30%), but the near-term trajectory is mixed. Q3 FY26 showed YoY revenue +7.4% and EPS +5.8%, yet QoQ trends are negative (revenue -4.4%, EPS -8.4%) with sequential margin compression. The company faces ~$1B after-tax oil cost headwind for FY27, $400M tariff impact in FY26, and a restructuring program targeting 7,000 job cuts. Valuation at 23x P/E sits near the lower end of its 1-year range (21.7-26.3), suggesting fair-to-slightly-cheap pricing vs own history, but not a compelling bargain given the headwinds. The upcoming Q4 FY26 earnings (late July) could be a modest catalyst, though guidance already points to the lower end of the $6.83-$7.09 core EPS range. Balance sheet is healthy with equity growing to $54.7B. The Thorne acquisition ($3.8B) signals strategic expansion into supplements but adds execution risk. Overall, a solid defensive holding with modest upside, but not enough mispricing or catalyst strength to warrant a higher score.
